question_type: two-group concentration index (HHI on value shares, and its reciprocal) from one as-of-dated commercial-bank ownership survey; survey as-of date vs bulletin issue month; index scale convention
decisive_step: Read 'survey ... published on the last day in 1959' as the Treasury Survey - Commercial Bank Ownership AS OF December 31, 1959, which is printed in the March 1960 issue (treasury_bulletin_1960_03.txt, section header at line 3013; Table 2 'Summary of Public Marketable Securities' header at 3038 with row 'Treasury notes' at 3044; Table 3 'Public Marketable Securities by Issues' header at 3085 with 'Total Treasury notes' at 3130), under the columns '16 New York City' and '14 Chicago'. The December 1959 issue has no NYC/Chicago breakdown and the June-30-1959 survey carries a different New York bank count, so the bank counts in the question single out the Dec-31 survey. Then compute HHI on 0-1 shares (the reciprocal definition rules out the 0-10,000 scale) and take the reciprocal of the unrounded index. Reference: worklog.md Step 0-1 (lines 8-27) and Step 4-5; review.md checks 1 and 3.

KEEP: find_tables' per-part 'as-of <DATE>' tag and the section name in the group label ('Table 3 in TREASURY SURVEY - COMMERCIAL BANK OWNERSHIP, DECE...'), which is how a[23]-[24], b2[26] and c[7]-[8] mapped 'last day in 1959' to the Dec-31 survey in the March 1960 issue; and show_table --grep on a plain row label, which at b2[30] returned the single needed row with both bank columns.

alternatives.change: printings: group by the part's as-of date as well as (part, column, period). Concretely, in otables.printings_page, key bycol on (part, ckey, period, asof) and print one SUMMARY block per as-of, e.g. '[as-of DECEMBER 31, 1959] part1 ... 14 Chicago: 1 printing' instead of '3 printings, 3 distinct values - REVISED/DIFFERS across printings' (a[32], c[25], b2[33]); and when the scan cap cuts, scan newest-first or centred on the pinned as-of/year, not oldest-first ('first 400 of 598 ... oldest issues first' drops exactly the later issues a revision check needs). The index already stores asof per part.
alternatives.why_not_first: no cell was misled here because the chosen survey happened to be the last one listed; but with the 'latest printing wins' sentence in AGENTS.md and the later_printing submit rule, a later semiannual survey sharing the same row and column labels would be offered as a 'revision' - a latent SOURCE_ISSUE_VINTAGE trap on any as-of-dated series.

notes: index.json links v8_analysis officeqa-divergence-analysis/per-question/041.json, but that file does not exist (all three v8 arms were correct; the v8 set only covers diverging questions) - only the v8 digests exist. The scale decision (0-1 vs 0-10,000) and 'reciprocal of the unrounded index' are the two places a cell could still go wrong; no text item covers them and all cells reasoned them out (a[35], c[36]); a single sentence 'when the question defines a derived quantity such as a reciprocal, choose the scale of the base quantity that makes the derived one sensible, and round only the final values' is cheap insurance. Every cell first looked in the December 1959 issue (a[10]-[18], b[14]-[20], b2[10]-[24], c[26]-[33]) before accepting that 'published on the last day in 1959' is the survey date; the tool listing's as-of tag is what ended each detour. Tool defects observed here and worth fixing before a learner evolves the tools: (1) printings groups cells by (part, column, period) only, so as-of-dated survey rows without a period collapse across surveys into 'REVISED/DIFFERS' (otables.printings_page, bycol key) and its 400-part cap scans oldest-first; (2) show_table --grep filters rows by label/period/section, so a column word returns 0 rows with no hint (c[10]) and a segment word returns every row of the segment (a[26]-[29]); (3) zero-byte, exit-0 tool output at c[14] (and b2[13] on ordinal 12) that reproduces correctly offline - a harness capture loss; (4) bare filenames resolve in show_table but not in sed/rg (c[16]), yet worked in cell b (b[25], b[29]) - workspace cwd differs between cells for an unknown reason; printing the absolute path in show_table's header line would remove the ambiguity; (5) the python helper's search/list_files return dicts and cost 2-3 steps in b and c (b[6]-[10], c[27]-[29]), as in v8.
